name: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg inside the historic Trier House documents the fascinating story of how a secluded mountain village became the cradle of Alpine skiing.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 6,00 €, Kinder in Begleitung frei
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Museum St. Anton am Arlberg is housed inside the charming Villa Trier, an Alpine Art Nouveau mansion built in 1912 set in peaceful parkland overlooking St. Anton am Arlberg. Originally constructed as an elegant mountain summer retreat, the building now serves as an intimate museum dedicated to the culture, Alpine settlement history, and winter sports heritage of the Arlberg region. St. Anton is universally recognized as the "cradle of Alpine skiing," where legendary pioneers like Hannes Schneider invented the Arlberg technique (stem christie) that transformed skiing into a global recreational phenomenon.

Route & Anforderungen

Visitors tour atmospheric, timber-panelled historic rooms spread over two floors. Exhibitions showcase the arduous lives of early mountain farming families, the engineering triumphs of the Arlberg railway and tunnel, and the founding of the historic Ski Club Arlberg in 1901. Highlights include vintage wooden skis, early leather bindings, period racing attire, and historical film footage of the famous Arlberg-Kandahar races. The surrounding park offers peaceful trails around a pond. While the park is level and accessible, the historic house features traditional wooden stairs. Allow 1 to 1.5 hours.

Besuch & Anreise

The museum opens during summer and winter tourist seasons in the afternoon and early evening (typically Sunday to Friday from 15:00 to 19:00; closed on Saturdays). Admission is around 6.00 Euro for adults, with accompanied children admitted free. From St. Anton railway station and town centre, a short scenic walk through the municipal park takes only five to ten minutes uphill. Parking is located in village car parks.

Tipps

The museum houses a top-tier restaurant with a panoramic sun terrace offering fine regional cuisine and spectacular views of Mount Galzig and the surrounding Arlberg peaks.
saison: Saisonal im Sommer und Winter nachmittags geöffnet
